strengths: Thorough empirical motivation: the paper carefully establishes a chain of evidence (visual complexity → attention entropy → accuracy degradation) using well-defined texture/color complexity metrics and correlates them with layer-wise attention entropy across many samples, providing a clear mechanistic story for why VLMs struggle in cluttered scenes.
The proposed CARVE method is simple, training-free, and requires no external tools (unlike SAM/YOLO-based approaches), making it broadly applicable and easy to integrate with existing VLM pipelines.

Extensive experimental validation: seven benchmarks, four base models (plus additional recent models Qwen3-VL and Gemma-3-27B in the appendix), multiple ablations (layer selection, time-step selection, mask hyperparameters, component ablation, decoding-strategy robustness), and comparisons against both training-free (ViCrop) and training-based (SD-RPN) baselines as well as external segmentation/detection tools.

Statistical rigor beyond simple point estimates: bootstrap confidence intervals and McNemar's tests are used to validate significance of gains on the smaller V* benchmark, which strengthens the empirical claims.

Honest and specific discussion of limitations, including a concrete qualitative failure case (BLINK relative-depth task) showing where the localized-masking approach removes necessary global context, which improves the credibility and completeness of the paper's claims.
Good reproducibility support: detailed algorithm pseudocode, hyperparameter settings, dataset configurations, and computational overhead analysis (GPU time/memory) are provided in the appendix.
weaknesses: The 'theoretical foundation' (Assumption 1, Theorem C.1–C.3) gives an appearance of rigor to what is essentially a heuristic ratio-based contrastive normalization; the 'existence and uniqueness' theorem is largely definitional (it assumes Fsem(G,I)=1 and then trivially solves for Fvis), and the convexity/closed-form derivations, while technically correct, do not provide non-trivial theoretical insight beyond justifying the chosen formula A^=A(Q)/(A(G)+λ). This formalism could mislead readers into overestimating the theoretical depth of the contribution.

CARVE requires three full/partial forward passes per query (general instruction, task-specific question, final inference on refined image), leading to roughly 2.5–3x GPU time overhead (Table 6) and added memory for attention storage; while mitigation strategies are analyzed, they remain largely theoretical projections (Appendix C.4) rather than implemented and empirically verified speedups.

Gains are highly uneven across models: very large on older/weaker models (e.g., LLaVA-1.5-7B: +27.8 pts on V*) but comparatively modest on stronger recent models (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL-7B: +8.9 pts on V*, and only +2.2% for Gemma-3-27B on TextVQA), suggesting diminishing practical utility as base VLMs improve, which tempers the significance of the contribution for state-of-the-art systems.

The comparison with external tools (Table 5, SAM/YOLO/CLIP) lacks methodological detail on how these tools were integrated into the masking/cropping pipeline, raising potential fairness concerns in that comparison.

The claim of 'no observed degradation of reasoning performance' is somewhat overstated given the appendix's own failure case on global spatial reasoning (BLINK depth task), where masking removes necessary contextual cues; this caveat should be more prominently integrated into the main text rather than relegated to a limitations subsection.

Several method hyperparameters (top-p threshold, K regions, layer range, time-step range, λ) require tuning, and the 'optimal' general instruction prompt was selected via grid search on TextVQA alone, raising minor concerns about generalization of these choices to other domains/languages not tested.

strengths: Well-motivated empirical analysis (Sect. 3) linking visual complexity (texture/color) to attention entropy and entropy to task accuracy, providing a clear rationale for the proposed method.
Training-free, model-agnostic approach that requires no external segmentation/detection tools and no additional training, making it easy to deploy across VLM families.
Extensive experimentation: seven main benchmarks, plus appendix evaluation on newer models (Qwen3-VL-2B/4B, Gemma-3-27B-it), showing the phenomenon and remedy generalize beyond the primary model set.

Thorough ablations covering time-step selection, layer-range selection, mask hyperparameters (p, K), and a component ablation isolating the contribution of contrastive normalization versus naive attention masking.
Comparisons against relevant baselines (ViCrop, SD-RPN, and external tools SAM/YOLO/CLIP) with both accuracy and latency reported, plus a reasonably fair OCR-free protocol for TextVQA.
Careful statistical validation on the small V* benchmark (bootstrap CIs and McNemar's test) strengthens confidence that gains are not due to sample-size artifacts.

Honest discussion of limitations, including a concrete failure case (BLINK relative depth) illustrating where localized masking removes necessary global context, and quantified inference/memory overhead.
weaknesses: The 'theoretical foundation' (Assumption 1's multiplicative decomposition) is a strong, largely unverified modeling assumption about real attention mechanisms; the appendix itself concedes the proofs 'characterize the idealized model... rather than exact properties of real attention,' making the abstract's framing of a rigorous theoretical contribution somewhat overstated relative to what is actually shown (mostly algebraic consequences of the assumption, not an independently validated theory).

The uniformity approximation for general-instruction attention is supported only by a single KL-divergence statistic on one model/dataset; robustness of this approximation across models, prompts, and complexity levels is not deeply investigated.

The method depends on several hand-tuned hyperparameters (layer range [20,25], time-step configuration, top-p threshold, K, and the specific general-instruction prompt chosen from 5 candidates), and while a 'unified configuration' is used across extended datasets, sensitivity to these choices for genuinely new models/tasks remains a practical concern.

Three required forward passes introduce non-trivial inference overhead (roughly 3x GPU time, higher latency than several baselines in Table 5); the proposed caching/early-termination savings in the appendix are analytical/asymptotic and not empirically demonstrated with wall-clock measurements.

Some of the largest reported gains occur for weaker/older baselines (e.g., LLaVA-1.5 on V*), which may partly reflect a low starting point/ceiling effect rather than a uniformly strong contribution; this is acknowledged but could be discussed more critically.

The method's own limitation analysis shows it can hurt tasks requiring global spatial context (e.g., depth ordering), constraining its scope to fine-grained/local-perception tasks, which is a meaningful boundary on the claimed 'general' visual reasoning enhancement.
